text: You find a new service, offering a free trial. Full access, risk-free for a month. Your amber stick-figure self is eager to explore this digital world.
But as you sign up, the system demands your credit card. A coral red flag appears. Why the card, if it’s truly free?
You search for a reason: perhaps it’s to verify you, or a security check? You input your card, accepting this friction.
The real reason is subtle: a core system design. This trial isn't just about trying; it's about setting up an automatic renewal default.
The cost: when the trial ends, the system automatically bills you. That small barrier to entry becomes a big barrier to exit. You pay before realizing.
Now you know. Next time a "free" trial asks for your card, you'll see the system. You're making an active decision, not just getting a trial.
